neet_phy_u09_t01_1.working: At constant pressure, work done on the gas is W = -PΔV = -(2×10^5)(2-5)×10^-3 = +600 J.

neet_phy_u09_t01_2.working: For isothermal compression, W_on = nRT ln(V1/V2) = 1×8.314×300×0.693 ≈ 1728 J ≈ 1.73 kJ.

neet_phy_u09_t01_3.working: For adiabatic compression, W_on = nRΔT/(γ-1) = 8.314×100/0.4 ≈ 2078 J.

neet_phy_u09_t01_4.working: Isochoric work is zero (I). Constant-pressure work is P(V2-V1) (II). Isothermal work on the gas is nRT ln(V1/V2) (III). Adiabatic work on the gas is (P2V2-P1V1)/(γ-1) (IV).

neet_phy_u09_t01_5.working: A is true. B is false: for the same compression ratio, adiabatic compression needs more work than isothermal. C is true. D is false: work done by the gas during compression is negative. E is true, since V1/V2 = P2/P1 for an isothermal process. So A, C and E.
